title: eval-harness: add per-prompt regression CI hooks and quality gating
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: we've seen regressions appear in downstream services due to prompt-variant specific quality degradations. This change introduces per-prompt evaluation hooks in CI that compute per-prompt metrics (accuracy/F1/semantic-similarity) and fail the build if any prompt's score drops beyond a configurable delta. Additionally, a quality gating layer is added to map eval metrics to CI pass/fail with a configurable alert threshold and an opt-in housewarming period.  What this PR does: 1) adds per-prompt metric computation and reporting to the eval-harness; 2) introduces a new CI job (eval/per-prompt-quality) that runs on PRs touching model-inference or prompts; 3) publishes per-prompt time series to metrics (prometheus/cortex) and attaches a summary artifact to the PR; 4) implements a lightweight rollback suggestion when a regression is detected (suggests previously-known-good model artifact id); 5) adds unit and integration tests for the new CI hook and the quality gating logic.  Compatibility and opt-in: the gating is opt-in via a repository-level config eval/config/prompt_quality.yml and defaults to alert-only for 7 days after enabling. Ops can flip to enforce mode once teams are comfortable. Backwards-compatible: default behavior for existing repos without the config file is unchanged (CI job runs in report-only mode).  Testing: added mock prompt-sets and golden outputs under eval/harness/testdata, unit tests for metrics aggregation, and an integration CI matrix that runs on node/py versions used in repo. Local runs on a staging CI runner were performed and artifacts attached.  Related: ENG-4218 (per-prompt scoring), ENG-4380 (qa gating policy), SUP-8921 (support ticket investigating prompt-specific regressions).
